statements.text: Can you discuss why the need for some of those higher standards in, you know, a higher standard of AI use framework in situations like that, and what some of the pitfalls are of not providing a higher standard for AI use in government than the private industry?
statements.context: Congressional hearing titled 'The Federal Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence,' where a member questions witnesses about standards for federal AI deployment.

statements.text: Do you believe that AI systems need independent oversight to ensure patients are not denied medically necessary care?
statements.context: Congressional hearing on healthcare affordability and technology, where the representative questions a witness about AI oversight in Medicare.

statements.text: It's scary for a lot of lawmakers. I've been in a lot of briefings where my colleagues can't really wrap their heads around the broad implications of what AI can do. Some people say, just (put) a moratorium on all of it. That isn't really going to work. [...] I don't know what the bill is yet. There are a lot of different ideas. A lot of things are moving forward this Congress, but it's not going to be just one policy.
statements.venue: Youth-focused town hall at Gig Harbor High School, answering a student question on AI regulation (reported by Gig Harbor Now)
